Ben / Steph — quick triage notes (ops):

- Scope: elevation confined to the Helix6b model pool serving us-east-1; no cross-region alerts. We see increased tail latency and token-serving 5xx on ~17–20% of requests for pinned helix6b:v2 during 07:40–08:50 UTC.
- Cause (initial): a mismatch in the dynamic batching window after a canary rollout earlier this morning caused a subset of low-priority jobs to monopolize batch slots, leading to backpressure and KV-cache thrashing on several hosts.
- What we did: rolled back the canary to previous batching config at 08:30 UTC, triggered auto-drain on affected instances, and forced a cold start of 12 hosts to clear KV cache.
- Current status: error rate reduced to ~3% by 09:00 UTC and has been trending down. No OOMs or node crashes recorded.

Attachments: helix6b-logs-20280422.txt (excerpt), telemetry-spike-graph.png

We recommend we:
1) Notify customer of mitigation completed and that we’re continuing to monitor for 8 hours.
2) Share postmortem draft and timeline once the team finishes log correlation.
3) Offer a small service credit if SLA threshold was crossed for NovaCorp’s committed usage.

I’ll continue to run log aggregation and push a PM rule to avoid similar batching changes without a staggered ramp.

Subject: Helix6b - follow-up & postmortem link

Hi all —

Final follow-up for today:
- Root cause: unintended batching-policy change introduced during a routine canary rollout. The new policy widened batching windows for lower-priority queues which allowed small requests to accumulate longer than intended; under peak traffic this caused KV-cache eviction churn and increased request tail latency leading to 503s.
- Impact window: 07:40–08:50 UTC (peak at ~07:53). Estimated affected requests: ~1.2M requests across NovaCorp’s pinned instances (18% failure peak).
- Remediation: rollback, host drain, cold-started instances, and a temporary hard-limit on batching window size for 48 hours.
- Preventative actions: stricter canary ramp schedule, automated rollback trigger for >5% 5xx in 5m, and a post-deploy validation test that simulates high tail-latency load.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix6b-incident
HubSpot: HS-4721

We recommend a modest service credit; Steph and finance can advise on amount tied to your committed usage. If OK, we’ll finalize and send the formal postmortem and credit proposal by 2028-04-23 end of day.

Marissa
